title: Classic Green Bean Casserole
subtitle: No holiday spread is complete without an old-fashioned green bean casserole.
intro: Green bean casserole is a staple at every holiday gathering in the South, from Thanksgiving to family potlucks. And while we love variations on a classic—like this slow-cooker green bean casserole—this five-ingredient traditional recipe is the one you should serve up every time you get the chance.
Learn how to make green bean casserole and also find some fun variations if you want to mix up the traditional side.

items: 2 (1-lb.) pkg. frozen haricot verts (extra fine green beans), thawed and squeezed dry
1 1/2 cups crispy fried onions (such as French’s), divided
2 oz. Parmesan cheese, grated (about 1/2 cup), divided

steps.title: Prepare oven and baking dish
paragraphs: Preheat oven to 350°F. Coat 11- x 7-inch baking dish with cooking spray.

steps.title: Combine ingredients
paragraphs: Stir together green beans, soup, heavy cream, 1/2 cup of the onions, and 1/4 cup of the cheese in a large bowl.

steps.title: Add casserole filling to baking dish
paragraphs: Transfer to an 11- x 7-inch baking dish. Top with remaining 1 cup onions and 1/4 cup cheese.

steps.title: Bake casserole
paragraphs: Cover with aluminum foil, and bake in preheated oven until casserole is hot throughout, about 20 minutes. Uncover, and continue to bake until cheese is golden, about 20 minutes. Remove from oven, and let stand 10 minutes. Serve.

sections.heading: Can You Use Canned or Frozen Beans in Green Bean Casserole?

blocks.content: Yes, you absolutely can use frozen, canned, or even fresh green beans in green bean casserole. This recipe calls for frozen green beans—as well as thawing and squeezing them to get out as much moisture as possible. If you’re going to use another kind, follow these tips:

content.text: These beans are already tender and cooked, so you only need to drain them before adding to the casserole mixture.

It’s a good idea to blanch fresh green beans before mixing them into the casserole. Cook the fresh green beans in boiling water for about 6 minutes, then stop the cooking process by moving them to ice water. They’ll finish cooking in the oven.
Thaw and drain frozen green beans. Then, squeeze them to remove as much moisture as possible. Frozen green beans are typically blanched before flash freezing, so they’re more tender than fresh.

sections.heading: How To Make Green Bean Casserole

blocks.content: This easy green bean casserole takes just 10 active minutes to prepare, so you can focus on the main dishes like spatchcocked turkey or baked ham.

content.text: Stir together the green beans, soup, heavy cream, and some of the onions and cheese. (If using fresh haricot verts instead of frozen, blanch them first.)
Transfer this mixture into a baking dish, topping with onions and cheese. Adding the grated Parmesan cheese before the fried onions allows it to melt better.

Cover the baking dish with aluminum foil, and bake it in the preheated oven for about 20 minutes Uncover it, and continue to bake until the cheese is golden, about another 20 minutes. Remove the dish from the oven, and let it stand for 10 minutes before serving.

sections.heading: How Do You Keep Green Bean Casserole From Becoming Mushy?

blocks.content: Two key steps will keep a green bean casserole from being too soggy:

content.text: Because canned green beans are pre-cooked, frozen haricot verts are a preferable option to keep this green bean casserole from getting mushy. In this dish, the crunch from the fried onions also serves as a perfect balance for the tenderness of the haricot verts after cooking.
If you choose a green bean casserole recipe that calls for fresh beans (instead of frozen as in this recipe), avoid overcooking them as doing so can result in an undesirably mushy texture.

sections.heading: How To Make Green Bean Casserole Ahead of Time

blocks.content: You can prepare this classic green bean casserole ahead of time, cover it with foil, and refrigerate it for about three days before baking. But leave off the crispy onions before storage.

If you will be baking after fridge storage, add a few minutes to the cook time to accommodate the temperature. Or let it stand for about 30 minutes at room temperature before baking. Be sure to add the crispy onions just before the casserole goes into the oven.
This simple five-ingredient green bean casserole is outstanding, but you can add a few things to it for additional flavor:

content.text: In place of Parmesan, try gouda, Swiss, or even Cheddar.
Make this a creamy broccoli casserole with blanched broccoli florets instead of the green beans.
Stir in mashed roasted garlic for loads more umami.
Cream of mushroom soup is iconic, but cream of celery or even cream of Cheddar soup would be great.
